# Runtime parameter-pattern first-source study

Prepared before executing these sources. This is an informed repository study,
not a blind model benchmark. The exact deployed model and sampling settings are
unrecorded. Available context includes the adopted ordinary type/linear owner
rules, common lexical IDs, current name-only runtime parameter parser, sized
projection, prior exact Unit-pattern implementation and its actual observations.

The desired next unit applies the shared exact pattern judgment to ordinary
function parameters without changing call arity, input type trees, effects,
owner identities or native rules. The current public Reference still describes
name-only ordinary parameters. These first sources are desired inputs, not an
assertion that their syntax or lowering has already been implemented.

Eighteen small sources are fixed: six desired forms, nine deliberate rejection
cases and three existing named-binder controls. Each complete source project
retains its Qargo edition. The largest quantum interface is two bits. No
maximum-size case, source-tree snapshot, Cargo build or Lean build is needed.

Finite check JSON and sized check stdout/stderr are separate observations.
Sized ordinary-classical lowering and product-basis limitations remain explicit;
a parse failure may mask their later diagnostics. No result is converted to
success. Sized native producer-consistency acceptance does not certify source
meaning. A subsequent independent Rust oracle must separate generic checking,
concrete elaboration, native acceptance and action.

The reused executable and checker are bound in identity-before.json, alongside
the prior Unit-pattern MSRV build records and current relevant source hashes.
This is not a fresh current-head build. Input sources and diagnostic bytes are
never repaired in place. Follow-ups must be separately named and explained.
